observation.description: The packaged runtime ships no persisted runtime-readiness receipt: @expo/snapback-runtime-darwin-arm64 contains only package.json, bin/snapback, and the Hermes framework, and running `snapback runtime-qualify` on the packaged binary prints a valid snapback.runtime-qualify.v1 result (restricted-no-eval-handler-vm, ok=true) but persists nothing. The repo-side discipline binds a digest-bound `<binary>.runtime-readiness.json` receipt that doctor and the proof rungs re-verify (LLP 0010); a public consumer has no receipt to pin and `runtime-qualify` appears nowhere in the guide, so the G1 'runtime-readiness identity' had to be reported from live command output.

competitorOutcome.description: No competitor offers a comparable handler-VM qualification receipt at all; this is a differentiator with an unfinished consumer-facing half rather than a parity gap.

mustNotRegress: doctor's live six-boundary qualification of the exact packaged binary — a persisted receipt must complement, never replace, on-demand qualification.
smallestCoherentFix: Document `snapback runtime-qualify` on the guide diagnostics page as the packaged readiness identity, and have doctor (or runtime-qualify with a flag) persist the digest-bound receipt under the app's managed .snapback/ state (not inside read-only node_modules) so consumers can retain it as evidence.
acceptanceWitness: An external consumer can produce and re-verify a digest-bound readiness receipt for the packaged binary via a guide-documented command; the guide page's snippet is CI-checked.
